text:
Rita (sales): Quick sync — Riverbank POC asked for sizing guidance. They said: peak traffic windows, multi-tenant, expected 95th latency target 300ms, mixed chat (70%) + embeddings (30%). Need recommended reserved GPU baseline, burst strategy, and an autoscale policy we can hand to them. Any immediate blockers?
Ryan (eng): Do we have traffic shape? peak qps, avg tokens per request, model family?
Rita (sales): They gave roughs: peak ~250 req/s during business hours, avg chat output ~120 tokens, embeddings tiny (~1-2 tokens). 24/7 but 3x peak during a 3-hour window. Model: prefer a 13B open model with 8-bit quantization.
Ryan (eng): Ballpark calc: 250 rps * 0.7 * 120 tokens ≈ 21k tokens/s from generation (chat) + embeddings negligible. For a quantized 13B on our runtime, one P100-class equivalent handles ~4-6k gen tokens/s depending on batch. So baseline ~4 GPUs to hit steady-state with headroom. For 3x peak burst = 12 GPUs if we want headroom for the 3-hour window.
Anya (infra): We usually recommend: reserve baseline (guaranteed) for the steady 95th capacity, and configure burst pool for spikes. Practical config: reserve 4 GPUs, configure autoscale to add +2 GPUs steps up to 8 via reserved-burst credits, and allow ephemeral spot/backfill to cover up to 12 if customer tolerates degraded latency.
Sam (pricing): From pricing POV: customer prefers predictable monthly commit but wants burst headroom. Offer: commit for 4 GPU-equivalents + 8 GPU-burst credits (time-limited) as an add-on. We can model oversubscription discounts; I'll draft numbers once engineering confirms final GPU class.
Maya (security): Heads-up: Riverbank pulled a security questionnaire. Must confirm: KMS integration, VPC peering for Private deployment, audit log retention, and whether embeddings are isolated or go through our shared pipeline. Also ask legal re: data retention SLA.
Rita (sales): Good call. They require customer-managed KMS and 1-year audit logs. Also want a runbook for fallbacks if reserved capacity is exhausted.
Ryan (eng): Fallback plan options: automatic model downgrade to a smaller quantized variant + degrade tail latency vs queueing requests. We can implement a policy: if queue depth > 50 for >30s OR 95th latency > 500ms, route to smaller model; else scale.
Anya (infra): Autoscale knobs we recommend: scale up when queued requests > 20% of baseline capacity OR 95th latency > 300ms for 45s; scale down after 10m below thresholds. Use incremental steps of 1-2 GPUs to avoid thrash. Also prewarm KV cache for expected heavy hours — schedule preheat 30m before predicted peak.
Rita (sales): Can we give them a short runnable load test they can run in POC to validate our numbers?
Ryan (eng): Yup — give them this simple sim snippet to run from their environment (just a headless throughput test):

```
# minimal bench script (toy)
python bench.py --target-url https://redwood-poc.example.com/generate --qps 250 --mix chat:0.7,embed:0.3 --avg-tokens 120 --duration 600
```

Change qps to test different peaks. We'll provide a Docker image if needed.
Sam (pricing): Also note: if they use Private deployment with customer-managed infra, pricing changes — flag the AM to confirm procurement timeline.
Maya (security): I'll answer the questionnaire items for KMS and logs; need a contact at Riverbank for SOC2 artifact exchange. Rita, can you intro?
Rita (sales): Intro going out after lunch. Also they asked about latency SLOs during burst — confirm whether can we promise 95th < 300ms during peak if they get reserved + burst credits?
Ryan (eng): With reserved 4 GPUs + burst up to 8 we can hit 95th < 300ms for their stated peak in most cases; for the 3x extreme window you'd need the full 12 GPUs or accept model downgrade to maintain latency. I'll add a short note for docs.
Anya (infra): Action items: 1) Ops playbook for preheat and KV warmups, 2) autoscale policy snippet, 3) recommended GPU counts + burst pack. I'll drop config snippets into the shared doc.
ops-bot: Checklist created: https://redwood.internal/checklists/riverbank-poc-capacity (items: baseline-reserve, burst-pack, autoscale-policy, security-answers, load-test-script) :white_check_mark:
Rita (sales): Great — I'll share this plan with Riverbank and loop back with their SOC contact. Any blockers on our side?
Ryan (eng): Nothing blocking. If Riverbank insists on strict 300ms SLO for 3x peak without extra GPUs, that's a negotiation point.
Sam (pricing): I'll prepare a commit+burst quote variant (4 baseline vs 6 baseline) and share numbers.
Maya (security): Send me their SOC contact and questionnaire PDF. I'll start drafting answers.
Rita (sales): Thanks all — ping me if you want me to schedule a 30m tech walk-through with Riverbank tomorrow. :)
